items.title: Introducing Vercel Schedules
items.summary: Cron jobs are useful for work that needs to happen regularly. You can use them to do things such as back up your database on a schedule, or keep data in sync between two systems.You define them once in code and then can update them by editing their config and redeploying. But today, agents interact with users as work evolves, and schedules need to be updated in real time.We built Vercel Schedules to allow agents and applications to create, change, or cancel one-time and recurring schedules through code, without redeploying.Schedules builds on the static approach used by , but are designed to let users and agents decide when work should happen while your application is still running. A schedule tells Vercel when to trigger a task and where to send it. Your application provides the code that carries out the work.Vercel Cron JobsYou can use schedules for both static and dynamic jobs:You can also test scheduled work on  before running it in Production.Preview deployments and in custom environmentsTake this example: A user could ask an agent with web access, “Tomorrow morning, summarize the top five stories on Hacker News.” The traditional solution would be storing the request and its schedule time in a database, then using a cron job to check for work that is due.With Schedules, an agent can create a schedule that records the request and when to run it, without a separate database and polling job. The example below defines an AI SDK tool that gives an agent this capability.When the task is due, Vercel uses  to deliver the saved request to your app. Your app provides , check the user’s current permissions, and start the agent. The agent fetches the top five Hacker News posts with a web tool, then returns a summary for your app to save for the user.Queuescode to read that requestIf you already build agents with  or , you can add a similar scheduling tool. The  uses Vercel Schedules to provide dynamic scheduling tools for production agents hosted on Vercel.fx’s JavaScript library, libfxPi’s agent libraryeve agent frameworkYou can schedule recurring work with Vercel Schedules. Schedules can be created dynamically via the , , and , or set up in your project’s configuration.JS SDKAPICLIFor example, to create a job that cleans up expired records every day, you could define a schedule that invokes a private function in your chosen time zone:Vercel calls this cleanup code directly, without exposing it at a public URL. It checks that each call comes from the scheduling service, so you don’t have to add that check yourself.If your app already uses the Nitro 3 server framework, its  lets you run the recurring jobs in your existing  configuration as private functions.experimental integrationscheduledTasksYou can also try the agent task and cleanup locally with , then test them on a Preview branch or in a custom environment before production.
